officials.name: Ken Cornell
officials.bio: Ken Cornell was born and raised in Gainesville, FL, and earned his Master's degree from the University of Florida. A small business owner and Certified Public Accountant, he was first elected to the Alachua County Commission in November 2014 and re-elected in 2018 and 2022. He is actively involved in various community boards and organizations.

officials.name: Charles "Chuck" Chestnut, IV
officials.bio: Charles "Chuck" Chestnut, IV holds a B.S. in Business Administration and an A.S. in Mortuary Science. He is a licensed Funeral Director and Life Insurance Agent. He previously served as a State Representative from 2006-2012 and a Gainesville City Commissioner from 2000-2006.

officials.name: Marihelen Wheeler
officials.bio: Marihelen has been married to Dr. Paul Wheeler for 25 years and is mother to 3 sons, also serving as a mentor and host family to many students. She has been involved with various local arts and environmental groups, including the Alachua County Education Association and Florida Wildlife Care. Her activist work includes 8 years dedicated to water quality and conservation, which led her to run for the Florida House of Representatives in 2012.

officials.name: Mary Alford
officials.bio: Mary Alford was first elected to the Alachua County Commission in 2020, after many years of volunteering in the community. She has served on various boards, including the Alachua County Environmental Protection Advisory Board and several local non-profit organizations. A sixth-generation Floridian, she holds degrees in Environmental Engineering from the University of Florida and is a recognized expert in sustainable design and energy-efficient homes.

officials.name: Anna Prizzia
officials.bio: Anna Prizzia is Commissioner for District 3 in Alachua County. She founded and currently oversees the UF/IFAS Field & Fork Program and works as the campus food systems coordinator for the University of Florida. With two decades of experience in sustainability efforts, she has worked with various non-profits and community organizations, and previously served in the Peace Corps.

officials.name: Clair Pease
officials.bio: Clair Pease represents Bay County Board of County Commissioners, District 5. A self-taught businesswoman, she has lived and worked in the community since 1993 and is currently the CEO of Emerald View Resorts. She is also passionate about protecting children and families, serving as an honorary board member for the Children's Home Society of Florida.

officials.name: Doug Crosby
officials.bio: Doug Crosby represents Bay County Board of County Commissioners, District 3. Elected in November 2024.

officials.name: Douglas Moore
officials.bio: Douglas Moore represents Bay County’s District 4, which encompasses most of unincorporated Bay County. Doug graduated from the University of Georgia in 1990 with a Bachelor’s of Business Administration in Finance, from Campbell University’s Norman Adrian Wiggins School of Law in 2006 with a Juris Doctorate, and from the Graduate School of Banking at Louisiana State University in 2014.

officials.name: Robert Carroll
officials.bio: Robert Carroll represents Bay County Board of County Commissioners, District 2. He and his wife Sharon have been married for over 20 years and are raising two daughters, Mia and Gianna.

officials.name: Andy Thomson
officials.address: 201 West Palmetto Park Road Boca Raton, Florida 33432
officials.bio: Mayor and CRA Chair, Andy Thomson was first elected to the Boca Raton City Council during a special election in August 2018 and secured re-election unopposed in March 2020. He was elected again in March 2024. He was elected as Mayor in March 2026. He is a product of Boca Raton – his parents met at Florida Atlantic University in 1967.

officials.name: Jon Pearlman
officials.address: 201 West Palmetto Park Road Boca Raton, Florida 33432
officials.bio: Jon Pearlman was elected to the City Council in 2026. Jon is a dedicated husband and father. He is a community advocate and his mission on the City Council is to put the residents first.

officials.name: Michelle Grau
officials.address: 201 West Palmetto Park Road Boca Raton, Florida 33432
officials.bio: A longtime Boca Raton resident, Michelle Grau has called the city home for more than 40 years. Driven by a commitment to represent the voice of the residents, she entered public office in March 2026 with a mission to safeguard the city's finances and promote transparency, accountability and responsible governance.

officials.name: Stacy Sipple
officials.address: 201 West Palmetto Park Road Boca Raton, Florida 33432
officials.bio: Stacy Sipple was elected to the Boca Raton City Council in March 2026. A fourth generation Boca Ratonian, she has deep roots in the community and a lifelong commitment to the city she proudly calls home. She is committed to protecting the city’s historical architecture, ensuring that the fate of public land is decided by public vote and attracting businesses that strengthen the community while supporting sensible, sustainable growth that respects Boca Raton’s history, residents, and quality of life.

officials.name: Yvette Drucker
officials.address: 201 West Palmetto Park Road Boca Raton, Florida 33432
officials.bio: A first-generation Cuban American, Council Member Drucker grew up in Miami and moved to Boca Raton in 2004. Council Member Drucker graduated from Florida International University with a degree in International Relations. As a corporate professional, she worked at ADP TotalSource for 13 years in Human Resources Management and Strategic Client Implementation.

officials.name: Vanessa Dragutinovic
officials.address: 9500 West Sample Road Coral Springs, FL 33065

officials.name: John Hearn
officials.address: 9500 West Sample Road Coral Springs, FL 33065

officials.name: Andrew B. Dunkiel
officials.address: 9500 West Sample Road Coral Springs, FL 33065

officials.name: Sherry Lynn Whitacre
officials.address: 9500 West Sample Road Coral Springs, FL 33065

officials.name: Daniel J. Alfonso
officials.address: 8800 SW 36th Street, Town of Davie, FL 33328
officials.bio: Daniel J. Alfonso was formally appointed as the District 2 Town Councilmember on February 18, 2026, and sworn into office on March 4, 2026. He also serves as the Executive Vice President of Business Services, Facilities Management and Public Safety at Nova Southeastern University (NSU) in Davie, overseeing various campuses and operations.

officials.name: Derrick L. Henry
officials.address: 301 S. Ridgewood Avenue Daytona Beach, FL 32114
officials.hours: Monday through Friday 8 AM to 5 PM
officials.bio: Derrick L. Henry, a Daytona Beach native, is serving his fourth term as mayor of the City of Daytona Beach, after running unopposed in 2024. He is the city's 21st mayor since 1926, when the towns of Seabreeze, Daytona and Daytona Beach merged into one city. Mayor Henry is our community's second African American mayor.

officials.name: Ben Preston
officials.bio: The Honorable Ben Preston is serving once again as Commissioner for District Two. He was first elected in July 2011, then again in March 2019. He is a 30-plus year resident of Deerfield Beach.

officials.name: Chris Nabicht
officials.bio: Commissioner Nabicht moved to Deltona in 1977 and served 31 years with the Deltona Fire District, retiring as Deputy Chief and Fire Marshal. He previously served eight years as District 6 City Commissioner and Vice Mayor. He holds an AS degree from Daytona State College and has been married for 40 years.

officials.name: Dori Howington
officials.bio: Dori Howington is the Commissioner for District 4, elected on November 11, 2024, with her term expiring in November 2028.

officials.name: Santiago Avila, Jr.
officials.bio: Mayor Santiago Avila, Jr. is the first Hispanic mayor elected in Deltona, FL, bringing Cuban and Mexican roots to his leadership. Since 2009, he has dedicated himself to building a stronger community through civic engagement and charitable work. Known as "The Constitutional Conservative," he advocates for constitutional awareness and inspires youth to pursue their dreams.

officials.name: Maritza Avila-Vazquez
officials.bio: Maritza Avila-Vazquez was elected Commissioner of District 3 in 2018 and chosen Vice Mayor in December 2021. She is a retired Executive Director and Vice-President from Republic National Bank of New York, where she managed their Technical Call Center. Since relocating to Deltona in 2000, she has been actively serving her community as a volunteer and leader.

officials.name: Andy Dance
officials.bio: Andy Dance represents District 1, which is within Palm Coast and includes the “E” section, “R” section, parts of the “W” section and Town Center. He serves on the following committees: Vice Chair of the Brevard Flagler Volusia Tri-County Consortium, Chair of the Flagler County Tourist Development Council, Vice President & Delegate of the Northeast Florida Regional Council, Volusia Flagler Transportation Planning Organization, School Planning Oversight Committee, Executive Board Member of the Small County Coalition of Florida, Transportation Disadvantaged Local Coordinating Board (Alternate).

officials.name: Gregory Hansen
officials.bio: Gregory Hansen represents District 2 in northeast Flagler County – including the Hammock and areas bounded by Interstate 95 and the ocean, and Beverly Beach north to the county line.

officials.name: Kim Carney
officials.bio: Kim Carney is Vice Chair of the Board of County Commissioners and represents District 3 in east Flagler County – including the municipality of Flagler Beach.

officials.name: Leann Pennington
officials.bio: Leann Pennington represents District 4, which includes the City of Bunnell and the areas west of U.S. 1. She is Chair of the County Commission and serves as a designee for the Family County Library Board of Trustees and the Heritage Crossroads Committee.

officials.name: Pam Richardson
officials.bio: Pam Richardson represents District 5, which includes the north area of Palm Coast and largely west of Interstate 95.

officials.name: John C. Herbst
officials.bio: Born in New York City, John C. Herbst is a veteran of the United States Marine Corps and holds a Bachelor's degree in Accountancy and an MBA. His diverse career spans investment banking, public accounting, and the insurance industry, and he previously served as the City Auditor for Fort Lauderdale, where he established the City Auditor's Office in 2006.

officials.name: Pamela Beasley-Pittman
officials.bio: Pam Beasley-Pittman is a tireless advocate of strengthening unity in her community, known for her integrity, diplomacy, honesty, and effective communication. A Fort Lauderdale native, she worked for the Broward County Sheriff's Office for 32 years, starting as a 911 Communications Operator and ending as an Extraditions Specialist.

officials.name: Steven Glassman
officials.bio: Steven Glassman was sworn in as Fort Lauderdale City Commissioner of District 2 on March 20, 2018, re-elected to a second term on November 3, 2020, and in 2024, he began serving his third and final term. Steve was born in New York City in 1953 and grew up on Long Island. After receiving his BA and EdM Degrees from SUNY Buffalo, he settled in Buffalo, New York where he was an educator for eighteen years.

officials.name: Dean J. Trantalis
officials.address:
1 East Broward Blvd
Floor 4
Fort Lauderdale, FL 33311
officials.bio: Dean Trantalis has proudly served as mayor of Fort Lauderdale since March 2018. He welcomes visitors to the city, known for its stunning coastline, rich cultural diversity, and endless opportunities for adventure, and is dedicated to creating a brighter future for all who call it home.

officials.name: Ben Sorensen
officials.bio: Ben Sorensen serves as the City Commissioner for Fort Lauderdale’s District 4. He brings a mix of enthusiasm for public service, faith, and military experience to his role. Ben is a steadfast advocate for ethical and transparent government, and he works diligently to ensure residents’ voices shape city priorities and progress.

officials.name: Darla Bonk
officials.bio: Darla Bonk grew up in Fort Myers, Florida and attended college in Tennessee, earning a degree in Communication and minoring in History and Bible. With more than 20 years of executive experience in corporate sales, operations, process implementation, planning, budgeting, and leadership development, Darla has worked with small business owners to CEOs, Founders, and Boards of major corporations. She was elected in November 2020 to serve as the Ward 6 councilperson and was re-elected in November 2024 for another 4-year term.

officials.name: Diana Giraldo
officials.bio: Councilmember Diana Giraldo took her oath of office for her four-year term after winning the Ward 2 general election. An architect, she is the founder and chief creative officer of a consulting firm dedicated to sustainable development solutions, green building certifications, and resiliency planning. She is also a tenured bicycle and pedestrian safety advocate and the first Latina ever elected to serve on the Fort Myers City Council.

officials.name: Fred Burson
officials.bio: Fred Burson is a native of Fort Myers, a licensed Real Estate Instructor, and Broker for Woodyard & Associates. He previously administered the City of Fort Myers STARS program and served as a youth baseball coach and Little League District Administrator. Currently, he is a Commissioner for the Community Redevelopment Agency and serves on several regional boards.

officials.name: Liston Bochette III

offices.name: City Hall
offices.address: 2200 Second Street Fort Myers, FL 33901

officials.bio: Liston “Lin” Bochette is a five-time Olympic Athlete, internationally recognized artist and civic leader. Councilman Bochette served on the Community Redevelopment Agency Board and, in 2018, was appointed to the Fort Myers City Council by Mayor Randall P. Henderson to complete the term of a retiring councilperson. He was elected to represent Ward 4 in November 2020 and re-elected in November 2024 for another 4-year term.

officials.name: Teresa Watkins Brown
officials.bio: Councilperson Teresa Watkins Brown began her career in telecommunications in 1975, retiring after 35 years of dedicated service in 2010. With 16 years of experience in local government, she was first elected to the City Council in 2009 and currently serves as Mayor Pro-Tem. She is deeply dedicated to working with people and serving the citizens of Fort Myers and the Ward 1 community.

officials.name: Terolyn Watson
officials.bio: Ward 3 Councilperson Terolyn Watson is a Fort Myers native and graduated from Fort Myers High School. Terolyn has worked for the Lee County School District for 26 years. She was elected as a member of city council in 2015. Currently, she is the assistant secretary of the National Black Caucus of Elected Officials. Watson loves to serve her community.

officials.name: Kevin Anderson
officials.bio: Kevin B. Anderson was sworn in as the 62nd Mayor of Fort Myers on November 16, 2020, after serving as Ward 4 councilperson for the previous two years. Mayor Anderson retired from Chico’s FAS, Inc. in June 2019 after 15 years. Prior to joining Chico’s, Anderson had a more than 24-year career with the Fort Myers Police Department, holding the rank of Major at retirement.

officials.name: Bryan Calvo
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010

officials.name: Gelien Perez
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010
officials.bio: Councilwoman Gelien Perez is a proud Cuban-American who was raised in the City of Hialeah, where she attended public schools and graduated from Hialeah Senior High School. She holds multiple degrees, including two Bachelor of Arts degrees from St. Thomas University and a Master of Science in Human Resources Management from Florida International University, and has over 11 years of dedicated public service with the City of Hialeah.

officials.name: Luis Gonzalez
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010
officials.bio: Born in Santa Fe, Cuba in 1970, Councilman Luis Gonzalez moved to Hialeah in 1981 and has called it home ever since. After pursuing accounting and earning a degree in Management, he worked in sales and launched a printing company before joining the City's Zoning Board in 2005. He served twelve consecutive years on the Hialeah City Council, including as Council President, and was elected President of the Miami-Dade League of Cities in 2012.

officials.name: Luis Rodriguez
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010

officials.name: Monica Perez
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010

offices.name: City Hall
offices.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010

officials.bio: Councilwoman Monica Perez was born and raised in our City of Hialeah. She earned a Bachelor’s of Science in Education from Florida International University and has a background in teaching. She was sworn into office as an elected official on November 8th, 2019.

officials.name: William Marrero
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010
officials.bio: William Marrero is a proud son of Hialeah, born and raised in the city he now serves as a City Councilman. A graduate of Hialeah Senior High School and a student of Public Administration at Florida International University, he has been involved in civic life from a young age. As a member of the Hialeah City Council, William is focused on delivering results for residents, supporting working families, and investing in safer streets and parks.

officials.name: Carl Zogby
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010
officials.bio: Councilman Carl Zogby was born in Union City, New Jersey, on March 9th, 1962. He is the third and youngest child of Cuban parents, who had migrated to the United States in the 1930s. His father was a World War 2 U.S. military veteran and his mother was a school teacher.

officials.name: Melinda De La Vega
officials.address: 501 President Donald J. Trump Avenue, Hialeah, Florida 33010
officials.bio: Councilwoman Melinda de la Vega was born and raised in the City of Hialeah. She earned a Bachelor’s Degree in Healthcare Management and has worked in health insurance for 20 years. Melinda is actively involved in her community and several nonprofit organizations, including the Hialeah Lions Club.

officials.name: Adam Gruber
officials.bio: Adam Gruber moved to Hollywood, Florida with his family from Montreal, Canada in 1978. He graduated from Hollywood Hills High School in 1992 and went on to earn a Bachelor of Arts and a Master of Science degree in Athletic Administration from Lynn University. He was first elected to the Hollywood City Commission in 2020 and has been an active part of the community for many years, dedicating himself to helping those in need through various charitable causes and community organizations.

officials.name: Caryl S. Shuham
officials.bio: Commissioner Caryl Shuham was born in Baltimore, Maryland and obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Civil Engineering from Johns Hopkins University. She went on to obtain her Juris Doctor from the University of Maryland and has worked as an attorney for more than 35 years representing companies engaged in the construction industry. She and her husband, Marty, are partners in the law firm of Shuham & Shuham, P.A. in downtown Hollywood.

officials.name: Idelma Quintana
officials.bio: Commissioner Idelma Quintana, born in rural Cuba and raised in Chicago, holds degrees from DePaul and Walden Universities. She has a long history of public service, including teaching, administration, and serving as Chief of Staff for Broward County Mayor Beam Furr. As a Hollywood City Commissioner, she focuses on economic development, sustainable prosperity, and community, having been re-elected for a full four-year term.

officials.name: Kevin Biederman
officials.bio: Commissioner Kevin D. Biederman has been a resident of Hollywood since 1985. He operates a successful Hollywood-based pest control business and previously served as a Commissioner with the Central Broward Water Control District. He is actively involved in the community, serving on various city committees and youth programs.

officials.name: Peter D. Hernandez
officials.bio: Commissioner Peter D. Hernandez was born in Havana, Cuba, and migrated to Madrid, Spain, before his family settled in Hollywood, Florida, as political refugees when he was eleven. He attended Apollo Middle School and McArthur High School, later earning his high school diploma and taking business classes at Broward College. As a small business owner, he has served on the Hollywood Commission for eight years and volunteered for several community boards and committees.

officials.name: Traci Callari
officials.bio: Vice Mayor Traci L. Callari has dedicated her career to public service, representing the residents of Hollywood’s District 3 since 2012. A proud resident of Hollywood since 1976, she holds a nursing degree and has a distinguished 20-year career at Memorial Healthcare System. She is also a proven leader in municipal and regional governance, serving on the Executive Board and Nominating Committee of the Florida League of Cities.

officials.name: Josh Levy
officials.bio: Mayor Josh Levy is deeply honored to have been re-elected to serve a third and final term as Mayor of the City of Hollywood, the community where he was raised. A proud graduate of Hollywood Hills High School, he earned a B.A. from the University of Florida and a law degree from Nova Southeastern University. His commitment to Hollywood began 26 years ago when he served as a law clerk in the City Attorney’s Office, followed by a twelve-year tenure on the city’s Planning & Zoning Board.

officials.name: Clemente Canabal
officials.address: City Hall 100 Civic Court Homestead, FL 33030
officials.bio: Canabal immigrated to the United States in 1994 with his family. He is a retired physician and entrepreneur who managed home healthcare agencies. He volunteers at several organizations in the Homestead community and resides in Capri, Isles At Oasis, with his wife, State Senator Ana Maria Rodriguez, and his children, JC, Nina, Hermes, and Eros.

officials.name: Larry Roth
officials.address: City of Homestead City Hall 100 Civic Court Homestead, FL 33030
officials.bio: Councilman Larry Roth was first elected to the City Council in November 2015. He grew up in Perrine/Palmetto Bay and moved to Homestead in 1990, falling in love with the community spirit after Hurricane Andrew. He has since served residents as a private citizen and Councilman, also co-founding the charity 'This Is For The Kids, Inc.'

officials.name: Sean L. Fletcher
officials.address: City of Homestead City Hall 100 Civic Court Homestead, FL 33030
officials.bio: Councilman Sean L. Fletcher was elected to Council Seat #2 in November 2019 and reelected in November 2023, having previously served 1999-2001. He is a former reserve police sergeant and trustee of the Police Officer Pension Board, and retired from Florida Power & Light after 30 years of service.

officials.name: Erica G. Ávila
officials.address: City of Homestead City Hall 100 Civic Court Homestead, FL 33030
officials.bio: Erica G. Ávila is a proud mother of three, military wife, business owner, and devoted resident of Homestead since 2009. For over 15 years, she has actively served the community through leadership in local associations, service organizations, and advocacy groups.

officials.name: Kimberly Konsky
officials.address: City of Homestead City Hall 100 Civic Court Homestead, FL 33030
officials.bio: A lifelong Homestead resident, farmer’s daughter, and Hurricane Andrew survivor, Councilwoman Konsky has dedicated more than 30 years to serving the community. She has volunteered thousands of hours with local nonprofits, civic groups, and schools, and has been actively involved in organizations such as the Homestead Woman’s Club, as well as community events including the Homestead Rodeo, Rotary Seafood Festival, and Kiwanis Prayer Breakfast.

officials.name: Steven D. Losner
officials.bio: Mayor Steven D. Losner was re-elected to a four-year term in November 2019 and 2021, having previously served on the Homestead City Council from 2001-2007. He has maintained a law practice in Homestead since 1992, focusing on estate planning, probate, corporate, and transactional representation. Losner is an active member of the Rotary Club of Homestead and has served on numerous community boards.

officials.name: Jenifer N. Bailey
officials.bio: Vice Mayor Jenifer N. Bailey was elected to a four-year term, unopposed, and also secured a two-year appointment as Vice Mayor in November 2025. She previously won re-election in November 2021 to a four-year term representing Council Seat #4. Vice Mayor Bailey is a dedicated advocate for youth development and the arts, serving on the Board of Together for the Children and actively supporting cultural enrichment.

officials.name: Shawn Sherrouse
officials.bio: On October 20, 2020, Shawn was selected as City Manager for the City of Lakeland. Prior to this appointment, he served as Deputy City Manager and as Assistant City Manager. Before his work with the City of Lakeland, Shawn was the Assistant City Manager for the City of Auburndale for four years and served as their Community Development Director for six years.

officials.name: Ashley C. Troutman
officials.bio: With nearly 20 years of experience in the financial services industry, Ashley Troutman is the Founder and Principal of Guided Financial Planning, guiding individuals and business owners through comprehensive financial planning and wealth management strategies. A lifelong resident of Lakeland, he is deeply committed to community service, serving as Chairman of the Board for Lighthouse Ministries and as a member of the Board of Trustees at Polk State College.

officials.name: Chad McLeod
officials.bio: Chad McLeod is in his second term on the Lakeland City Commission and has been serving since 2020. He is a Polk County native and fourth-generation Floridian. As a commissioner, Chad chairs the Finance Committee and serves on the Real Estate and Transportation, Affordable Housing Advisory and Legislative committees, and Polk County’s Tourist Development Council.

officials.name: Guy LaLonde Jr.
officials.bio: Guy LaLonde Jr. serves as City Commissioner for the Northwest District for the City of Lakeland, Florida. A United States Navy veteran, business owner, and community leader, he brings decades of leadership experience in business operations, financial management, and public service. Born and raised in New Hampshire, Guy moved to Lakeland in the 1980s and proudly made the city his home.

officials.name: Mike Musick
officials.bio: Mike Musick is the owner of Musick Construction & Roofing and has lived in Lakeland for more than 40 years. He is a 1991 graduate of Lakeland Christian School (LCS), where he won multiple state championships as a member of the track team. For the past 12 years, Mike has coached cross country and track at LCS.

officials.name: Sara Roberts McCarley
officials.bio: Sara Roberts McCarley was born in Lakeland, raised in Davenport, and graduated from Florida Southern College. She has dedicated her career to making a meaningful difference, serving in various leadership roles including Chair of the Citrus Connection and Mayor of Lakeland since January 5, 2026. Following the passing of her first husband, Randy, she founded the Randy Roberts Foundation to empower young people in government.

officials.name: Stephanie Madden
officials.bio: Stephanie Madden is a small business owner and Lakeland City Commissioner. She and her husband, Steve, started ShopMadden, a promotional marketing company in 1995. Stephanie is a mother to six children and a grandmother.

officials.name: Terry G. Coney
officials.bio: Terry G. Coney is a proud son of Lakeland, a 22-year Air Force veteran, and holds degrees from Florida A&M University and Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University. He has a strong record of community service, including leadership roles at First Baptist Institutional Church and extensive volunteer work on city and county boards and committees. His goal is to improve the quality of life for all citizens of Lakeland.

officials.name: Rob Hernandez
officials.bio: Rob Hernandez began his municipal government career in 1994, holding various leadership roles including Deputy County Administrator for Broward County and City Manager for several cities. He is a 23-year US Army Reserves veteran, holding a Master’s in Public Administration from Nova Southeastern University and a Bachelor's from Florida International University.

officials.name: Bill Proctor
officials.bio: Commissioner Bill Proctor has served the citizens of District 1 since 1996. He represents the central city and southside areas of Leon County District 1, and his priorities include affordable housing, quality healthcare, education, and economic development. Commissioner Proctor has also served as Chairman of the Board in 2006 and 2015.

officials.name: Brian Welch
officials.bio: Commissioner Brian Welch has served the citizens of District 4 since 2020. He was elected to the Leon County Commission in November of 2020 to represent the residents of Northeast Leon County. Brian’s priorities include protecting the quality of life and property values of neighborhoods, providing adequate recreational and transportation infrastructure, protecting the environment, and keeping communities safe.

officials.name: Carolyn D. Cummings
officials.bio: Commissioner Carolyn D. Cummings has served the citizens of Leon County since 2020. She was elected to the Board of County Commissioners on November 3, 2020, and holds a Juris Doctorate from the University of Florida Law School. A Leon County resident for over thirty years, she has been a practicing attorney in both public and private sectors.

officials.name: Christian Caban
officials.bio: Christian Caban was elected to the Leon County Commission to represent District 2 in 2022 and currently serves as 2025-2026 Chairman. He is most passionate about serving the best interests of District 2 by prioritizing public infrastructure, economic development, community safety, youth services, and environmental issues.

officials.name: David T. O'Keefe
officials.bio: Commissioner David O’Keefe has served the citizens of Leon County since 2022 and currently serves as 2025-2026 Vice Chairman. Elected in 2022, he previously spent fifteen years overseeing finances for public nonprofits and government organizations. A licensed Certified Public Accountant, he holds degrees from Florida State University and Auburn University and volunteers for various community programs.

officials.name: Nick Maddox
officials.bio: Commissioner Nick Maddox has served the citizens of Leon County since 2010. As the CEO of Family Promise of the Big Bend and Chair of the esteemed Leon County Commission, Nick has proven himself as a visionary leader with a heart of gold, determined to bring about real change and uplift those in need.

officials.name: Rick Minor
officials.bio: Commissioner Rick Minor has served the citizens of District 3 since 2018. He was re-elected in 2022 and is focused on growing the economy, reducing crime, protecting the environment, and ensuring high ethical standards in local government. He also works on projects to improve infrastructure and amenities in northwest Leon County.

officials.name: David Neuman
officials.bio: David Neuman represents Melbourne’s District 3. He was elected to the Melbourne City Council in November 2024. He also serves on the Airport Authority Board and is an alternate member of the Space Coast Transportation Planning Organization. His current term extends to November 2028.

officials.name: Julie Kennedy
officials.bio: Vice Mayor Julie Kennedy was first elected to the Melbourne City Council in 2018 and re-elected in 2022 to represent District 6. She holds a bachelor's degree in psychology and elementary education and a master's in educational leadership, having worked for Brevard Public Schools since 1996. Currently a building administrator at Brevard Adult and Community Education, she also serves as president of the Space Coast League of Cities.

officials.name: Marcus Smith
officials.bio: Council Member Marcus Smith represents Melbourne's District 1 and was elected in November 2024, bringing over 30 years of leadership experience as a retired U.S. Air Force Lieutenant Colonel. He previously served on the Melbourne Planning and Zoning Board and holds an MBA and a Bachelor's in Electrical Engineering. Committed to workforce development, infrastructure improvement, and civic engagement, he advocates for smart, sustainable growth for Melbourne.

officials.name: Mark LaRusso
officials.bio: Council Member Mark LaRusso was first elected to office on November 6, 2018, and was re-elected on November 8, 2022, by the city at large to serve on the Melbourne City Council as the representative of District 2. His current term extends to November 2026. He served as Vice Mayor from November 2022 until November 2023.

officials.name: Mimi Hanley
officials.bio: Mimi Hanley was elected to office on November 3, 2020, and was re-elected on November 5, 2024, by the city at large to serve on the Melbourne City Council as the representative of District 5. Her current City Council term will continue until November 2028. She is a member of the Space Coast Transportation Planning Organization.

officials.name: Rachael Bassett
officials.bio: Rachael Bassett was elected to the Melbourne City Council as the representative of District 4 in November 2022, serving a four-year term. She holds certifications as a Florida Realtor, Private Investigator, and Security, and is a member of the Florida Association for Private Investigators and a lifetime member of the NRA. Bassett actively volunteers in the community, focusing on lagoon and neighborhood improvements, and is a voting delegate for the Space Coast League of Cities.

officials.name: Paul Alfrey
officials.bio: Paul Alfrey is the Mayor of the City of Melbourne, elected in 2020 and re-elected in 2024, after previously serving as Vice Mayor and Council Member for District 5. He is also an entrepreneur and multiple small business owner, as well as a member of the Melbourne Orlando International Airport Authority Board and the Melbourne Affordable Housing Board.

officials.name: George Wysong
officials.bio: George K. Wysong, III was appointed as the City Attorney for the City of Miami in April 2024. He began his career with the City as an Assistant City Attorney in November 1994, and has dedicated the majority of his professional life to representing Miami in numerous practice areas. During his time with the Office of the City Attorney, Mr. Wysong has gained extensive experience in nearly every facet of municipal law.

officials.name: James Reyes
officials.bio: City Manager James Reyes was sworn in as the new City Manager on January 12th, 2026, nominated by City of Miami Mayor Eileen Higgins. As City Manager, James is the city’s chief administrative officer, overseeing daily operations, more than 5,000 employees, and a $1.8 billion budget. Prior to this role, he served as Chief of Public Safety for Miami-Dade County and held senior leadership positions with the Broward Sheriff’s Office.

officials.bio: City of Miami District 5 Commissioner Christine King is passionate about serving the public and has been since an early age. She represents Liberty City, Little Haiti, Model City, Overtown, Wynwood/Edgewater, and the Upper East Side. In November 2021, she became the first Guyanese American to be elected in the City of Miami and the first female to be named Chairwoman of the Commission.

officials.name: Damian Pardo
officials.bio: District 2 Commissioner Damian Pardo was elected to represent District 2 in the City of Miami in November 2023. A lifelong resident of District 2, he has been a community activist for over 35 years, advocating for equality, diversity, and inclusion in South Florida.

officials.bio: Ralph Rosado is a dedicated public servant and proud Miami native, now serving as the City of Miami Commissioner for District 4, which includes the neighborhoods of Flagami, West Flagler, Little Havana, Coral Gate, Shenandoah, Golden Pines, and Silver Bluff. A graduate of Belen Jesuit Preparatory School and Florida International University, he was both educated and shaped by this community. Today, he is raising his three children in the heart of the district he now represents.

officials.name: Rolando Escalona

offices.name: Little Havana
offices.address: 1300 SW 12th Avenue Miami, FL 33129

officials.bio: District 3 Commissioner Rolando Escalona serves as the City of Miami Commissioner for District 3, representing diverse and historic neighborhoods. Elected in December 2025, Commissioner Escalona brings a new generation of leadership focused on accountability, accessibility, and delivering real results for residents. Born in Havana, Cuba, he was raised in Miami, and his story reflects resilience, hard work, and opportunity.

officials.name: Eileen Higgins
officials.bio: Mayor Eileen Higgins is the first woman elected Mayor of the City of Miami. She leads a results-driven administration focused on building a safer, more connected, and more resilient city where working families can thrive. Her priorities include accelerating housing delivery, modernizing infrastructure and mobility, strengthening neighborhood services, supporting small businesses, and reforming City Hall to operate with clear standards, transparency, and measurable results residents can see and feel.

officials.name: Avril Cherasard
officials.bio: Backed by a strong academic foundation and professional experience across public service, real estate, and finance, she brings a well-rounded and solutions-driven approach to leadership, policy development, and community engagement, ensuring meaningful impact throughout the community.

officials.name: Maxwell B. Chambers
officials.bio: Maxwell B. Chambers immigrated to the United States from the hills of Clarendon, Jamaica, and has been a resident of the beautiful City of Miramar since 2007. He was first elected to office in 2015 as Commissioner in the City of Miramar, became Vice Mayor in 2016, and was re-elected in March 2017 and 2021, currently serving as Commissioner.

officials.name: Yvette Colbourne
officials.bio: Commissioner Colbourne represents District 5 and is currently the Chair. She was awarded the “Complete Streets Champion Award” during the 2023 Safe Streets Summit, for being an exceptional leader and catalyst in advancing Complete Streets in Broward County. Under her leadership as Chair, the Broward MPO adopted its 2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan (MTP) creating a road map for the future vision of transportation not only in Miramar but also for the entire Broward County region.

officials.name: Wayne M. Messam
officials.bio: Mayor Wayne M. Messam is a proud first-generation American, born to Jamaican parents and raised in South Bay, Florida. A lifelong athlete and leader, he earned a full athletic scholarship to Florida State University (FSU), where he excelled both academically and athletically. As a wide receiver, he was a member of the 1993 National Championship football team under Coach Bobby Bowden and later played briefly in the NFL with the Cincinnati Bengals.

officials.name: Carson "Eddy" Edwards
officials.bio: Meet Carson "Eddy" Edwards: A dynamic entrepreneur, community advocate, and champion for progress. With roots in Kingston, Jamaica, and a leadership-driven spirit, Eddy brings decades of experience and a relentless drive to make a difference in Miramar. His extensive involvement in business, community, and civic engagement showcases his dedication to enhancing the lives of those around him.

He has served as a Fort Walton Beach City Council member (2011-2014) and as County Commissioner for District 4 since November 2014, also serving as Chairman in 2023 and 2026. Additionally, Commissioner Goodwin is a personal watercraft safety advocate and lives in Fort Walton Beach with his family.

With a distinguished two-decade career in Aerospace and Defense, he holds multiple degrees and certifications. As Commissioner, he is committed to driving economic development, improving infrastructure, maintaining low taxes, and enhancing county services.

With over 38 years as an Okaloosa County resident, she brings extensive federal, state, and local experience in social services policy and administration. She was recognized as Florida's Social Worker of the Year in 2015 and received the 2020 Presidential Advocacy Award from the Florida Association of Counties.

He was elected in August 2020 and took office in November 2020 for a four-year term. Outside of his duties, he serves as a Pastor at Central Baptist Church in Crestview and is committed to responsive, ethical government that protects the quality of life.

officials.bio: Commissioner Sherri Cox is a lifelong resident of Northwest Florida, dedicated to defending constitutional rights and economic opportunity while preserving the region's culture and natural beauty. She holds degrees in Music Performance and Chemistry, and has a successful career in business, political, and real estate development consulting. Deeply rooted in public service, she serves on various committees and is committed to enhancing Okaloosa County's quality of life and economic opportunity.

officials.bio: Ann moved to St. Johns County in 2013 and enthusiastically traded Arizona’s deserts for our beautiful beaches. But her conservative roots run as deep as the Grand Canyon. Ann earned a Bachelor of Science Degree in Business at Arizona State University which she attended on an academic scholarship.

officials.name: Christian Whitehurst
officials.address: 500 San Sebastian View, St. Augustine, FL 32084
officials.bio: A life-long Floridian, Christian Whitehurst has been a part of the Northwest St. Johns County community for over twenty years. As a job creator and business owner, he focuses on economic development, infrastructure, and core services, while also supporting youth, veterans, law enforcement, and first responders. He believes communication is key to serving the community at the highest level.

officials.name: Clay Murphy
officials.address: 500 San Sebastian View, St. Augustine, FL 32084
officials.bio: A resident of St. Johns County for over 33 years, Commissioner Murphy is married to Pamela and they have three children and six grandchildren. He served as a Florida State Trooper for 26 years and is now the owner and operator of a local Sonny’s BBQ. He is also active in local charities and has served his church for over 30 years.

officials.name: Krista Joseph
officials.address: 500 San Sebastian View, St. Augustine, FL 32084
officials.bio: Krista Joseph has lived in Florida since 2007, ten of those years in St. Johns County. She previously served on the Citrus County Hospital Board, helping to turn around a failing hospital. A mother of five, including two U.S. Navy SEALs, Krista is an award-winning author and a frequent speaker to local organizations.

officials.name: Sarah Arnold
officials.address: 500 San Sebastian View, St. Augustine, FL 32084
officials.bio: Sarah Arnold was appointed by Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis in 2021 to serve on the BOCC and was later elected in 2022. She is invested in the St. Johns County community, its schools, its development, and its future, and serves on several boards and volunteers with local organizations. A lifelong Floridian, she and her husband raise their four children in District 2.

officials.name: Kenneth T. Welch
officials.bio: Kenneth T. Welch is the Mayor of St. Petersburg. He is a third generation St. Pete resident, father of two daughters, a graduate of THE Lakewood High School, a fan of the SunRunner and a strong believer that if we keep our eye on Inclusive Progress - it will always lead the way. As Mayor, Ken is working to make St. Pete a city for everyone through his guiding Principles of Accountable Government and Pillars for Progress. You'll often hear him say...."We Are St. Pete!"

officials.name: Kali Dambeck
officials.office: Special Assistant – Chief of Staff Doyle Walsh

officials.name: Curtis Richardson
officials.bio: Curtis Richardson, Mayor Pro Tem - Seat 2, was born in Jacksonville and reared in Green Cove Springs, Florida. He graduated with honors in 1974 and obtained a B.S. degree in Psychology from Florida State University, later earning a Masters degree in Counseling Psychology from the University of West Florida and a Master's degree in School Psychology from FSU. His career in public service began with his election to the Leon County School Board in 1990, followed by election to the Florida House of Representatives in 2000.

officials.name: Dianne Williams-Cox
officials.bio: Commissioner Dianne Williams-Cox was born and raised in Quincy, Florida, and graduated with honors from Florida A&M University with a B.S. in Data Processing Technology. She also holds a Master’s in Business Administration from Nova Southeastern University. Her life has been dedicated to community service, voter advocacy, and championing causes for underserved residents in Tallahassee.

officials.name: Jacqueline "Jack" Porter
officials.bio: Jack was born and raised in São Paulo, Brazil and later moved to South Florida, where she lived until moving to Tallahassee to attend Florida State University. As a longtime community builder, Jack has worked tirelessly to advance progress on the issues that matter to our neighborhoods. Most recently, Jack worked at the Florida Department of Environmental Protection as a Florida Gubernatorial Fellow.

officials.name: Jeremy Matlow
officials.bio: Raised on Tallahassee’s south side, Commissioner Jeremy Matlow was elected to City Commissioner in 2018, advocating for citizens and neighborhoods to drive City Hall's priorities. He co-founded Gaines Street Pies and serves on various agencies including the CRA and Capital Regional Transportation Planning Agency.

officials.name: Reese Goad
officials.bio: Reese Goad has worked for the City of Tallahassee for more than 26 years. Prior to being appointed as Tallahassee's City Manager in September 2018, Goad served as the interim City Manager and the Deputy City Manager. Goad has fostered a culture within the organization focused on ethics and delivering high quality, affordable municipal services.

officials.name: John E. Dailey
officials.bio: Mayor Dailey has dedicated his professional life to building strong, vibrant communities. He began his career working for the Florida League of Cities and the National League of Cities. After founding JDA Strategies, he was elected to the Leon County Commission in 2006 and then Mayor of the City of Tallahassee in 2018.

officials.name: Jane Castor
officials.bio: Mayor Jane Castor, the 59th Mayor of the City of Tampa, is a lifelong resident who served as Tampa's first female Chief of Police before being elected mayor in 2019. She was overwhelmingly reelected in 2023 and focuses on improving residents' quality of life through infrastructure, housing, and sustainability initiatives.

officials.name: Keith A. James
officials.address: 401 Clematis Street West Palm Beach, FL 33401
officials.bio: Keith James was first elected Mayor of the City of West Palm Beach on March 12, 2019, and re-elected, unopposed, to a second four-year term in 2023. As Mayor, he has focused on building a "Community of Opportunity for All" by expanding affordable and workforce housing, strengthening public safety, and investing in infrastructure. Mayor James is the City of West Palm Beach's first African-American "strong mayor," serving as the City's Chief Executive Officer and directing its administrative operations.
